definition.def: You use precise to emphasize that you are referring to an exact thing, rather than something vague. [emphasis]
examples: At that precise moment I felt sorry for him and didn't want to hurt him.
The precise location of the wreck was discovered in 1988.
He was not clear on the precise nature of his mission.
We will never know the precise details of his death.

definition.def: Something that is precise is exact and accurate in all its details.
examples: He does not talk too much and what he has to say is precise and to the point.

definition.def: You say 'to be precise' to indicate that you are giving more detailed or accurate information than you have just given.
examples: More than a week ago, Thursday evening to be precise, she was at her evening class.
The restaurant in which we ate that night had more people in it at 11pm, 51 more to be precise, than it did at 10pm.
